title: Cocycle pairing and ordinary-tensor augmentation on a ringed site
statement: Work in a common coefficient universe with small sites [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let R be a sheaf of commutative rings and use its module sheaves and ordinary tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and a representative-normalized derived tensor T as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation], [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. K-flat complexes and their signed total tensor are those of [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For any U,V in D(R) and integers p,q, define the unique morphism H^p(U) tensor_R H^q(V) to H^{p+q}(T(U,V)) characterized as follows: for every pair of flat-term K-flat representatives P,Q and isomorphisms Q(P)=U, Q(Q)=V, the tensor of cycles maps into cycles of the signed total tensor in its (p,q) summand, and after quotienting by boundaries the pairing sends [x] tensor [y] to [x tensor y], transported by the given canonical representative comparison. This is a statement on sheaf morphisms, so the formula is sheafified. For R-modules F,G, define the degree-zero total-tensor map Tot(F[0] tensor G[0]) to (F tensor G)[0] by the usual identification in the (0,0) summand. Define the unique augmentation T(F[0],G[0]) to (F tensor G)[0] whose pullback along every pair of quasi-isomorphisms P to F[0] and Q to G[0] from flat-term K-flat complexes is the localization of their total tensor followed by that degree-zero identification. No flatness of F or G is assumed.
